current.text: He is a projected starter at center, next to VanVleet, Thompson, Durant and Smith.
Coach Ime Udoka has blamed his defense for years. He sometimes plays other bigs over Sengun, which limits his minutes.
Houston has more guard depth now, so his minutes could drop from 33 to about 31 or 32.
Fred VanVleet is back. His absence boosted Sengun's assists.
His assists will likely fall to 5 to 5.5 with VanVleet back. He had his best shot-blocking year last season, so blocks have no upside to make up for it.
Houston added shooting coach Chip Engelland to its staff. He seemed afraid to shoot threes last season.
Engelland may help his outside shooting.

Experts disagree on his draft cost. Lloyd calls his ADP reasonable and ranks him 24 to 30 in category leagues, and Josh puts his auction value close to 30 USD. Others say drafters take him too early, possibly swayed by a preseason triple-double, and one expert regretted taking him at pick 22.
He is alone in tier four of the center rankings. You could reasonably take him ahead of Towns or even Barnes.
With our March 28 end, Houston has a weak 3-3-4 fantasy playoff schedule: 10 games over weeks 19 to 21.
Houston has only 14 back-to-backs this season.
Houston is projected to win 54 games. The team is expected to play it safe in the regular season and not chase seeding.

durable.text: He is a two-time All-Star who can put up about 20 points, 10 rebounds and 5 assists.
He is a poor free throw shooter on real volume. FT% is his worst category.
He gives guard-like assists from the center spot. Steals and blocks plus over six assists make his stat line unusual.
He commits many turnovers, clearly more than other forwards and centers.
He makes very few threes, and his three-point shot will probably never come around.
He is not a big shot blocker. Experts differ on his steals, from decent to little help.
He helps FG% on good volume. His weak spots are finishing at the rim, overall efficiency and too many low-percentage mid-range shots. He also complains to officials a lot.
His defense is a concern, and that matters under a defense-first coach who gives little room for error.
He is worth more in points leagues than in category leagues.
Last season he missed time with back tightness and then an ankle injury. He wore down in midseason after playing EuroBasket.

note: Yahoo values him at 32 USD and ESPN at 25 USD. Both average costs are about 33 USD, and he cost 36 USD in our league last season, so the market pays above the 30 USD that experts and the ESPN value suggest. He fits punt FT% and punt TO builds best, where his assists from center (z +2.3 vs position), rebounds and FG% count fully and his 69% FT and 3 turnovers do not hurt. Early in the season, check whether his minutes slip to 31 or 32 under Udoka and whether his assists fall toward 5 with VanVleet back. Houston's 10-game playoff schedule is also weak.
